correctness.rationale: Essential spectral tails provide infinite-dimensional coefficient subspaces with uniform lower bounds. Explicit rank-one column/row spaces and contractive block projections give 1-complemented Hilbertian input and output witnesses. Direct arguments for approximation, Bernstein, Gelfand and Kolmogorov numbers, together with the defining obstruction for strictly singular operators and compact-factor approximation, establish the stated lower bounds and exact cases.

originality.rationale: Qualitative compactness and strict-singularity results for multiplication operators, including basic restriction statements for compact-operator spaces, are treated as prior art. Targeted searches did not locate the exact all-index four-s-number flatness for one-sided multiplication on arbitrary normalized symmetrically normed Banach ideals, the exact K/FSS/SS distances, or the two-sided essential-norm floor with compact-factor asymptotics. Residual risk from older elementary-operator and norm-ideal literature remains, so the claim is to the best of our knowledge.

value.rationale: The theorem turns a simple rank-one geometric mechanism into simultaneous sharp information for four classical s-number scales and three operator-ideal distances across all normalized symmetric Banach ideals of compact operators, with an especially strong flat profile for one-sided multiplication.
